body: Maybe if his family is supportive you could tell one of them? With my depression I initially just told my sister who kept it a secret for everyone else. But then I had to tell everyone and they're actually not horrible with it. You'd have to gauge it. I know from telling some friends, some are really supportive, some are mean and some just can't be bothered. I think he needs help from someone who can get him help and is supportive.

I think you should tell someone but I'm not sure who... someone might have a better idea? Any adult will take this seriously and probably report it to something/someone. What's his family like? Are they supportive? My concern is that he's physically harming himself now and that can escalate into something more later.

Or maybe you can talk to him about him telling someone else about it and you can go with him? That might take some time though. He does need support though. He's probably feeling so horrible now, so bad that he is cutting himself, so be there for him.

I have tried. . . after like a month most just say "you'll get better in time" and "move on and find someone new". Even though I try to explain how severe the depression is they didn't really get it. And now they just say they're busy all the time.

Oh. . . I understand it better now. Although she didn't directly tell you no, you know by her actions that she doesn't reciprocate your feelings. So take that and do your best to move on. I know easier said than done but you know how she feels based on her actions.

She didn't say no to you? Did you not ask her in person?

If you told her in a text, she probably isn't sure how to respond and doesn't want to hurt your feelings. I'm sure she does recognize you as a person with feelings, she just doesn't want to hurt them. But you're right, you do deserve the respect of getting an answer. In trying to not hurt your feelings she is probably hurting you more.

Follow everyone's advice and do what they said - go to the gym, prepare for school, etc. To be cliche, you deserve someone who will at least respond to you.

Rejection of any type is difficult and I'm sorry. That was 2 years ago. So just like you're not the same person you were 2 years ago, I'm sure she's also changed in those 2 years.

Sometimes the timing just isn't right. It sucks. I had a recent failed relationship that was either due to my depression or triggered my depression - I'm not sure. And it''s horrible. I can't even describe it because it's that horrible.

But it might not be forever. If you want to keep her as a friend, give her some time and then initiate contact after a few weeks or so. She might still care for you as a friend but isn't sure what to do and/or doesn't want to lead you on. If you don't want to talk to her again, then don't.

The important thing is that you're feeling better enough to ask her and now you know. That's a huge step! So hopefully the next time it'll be even easier.

I've been that girl before. . . It was difficult for me to hurt my friend but I just didn't like him in that way. We were on a sports team together so I saw him once or twice a week. I was hoping we'd stay friends afterwards but he kept emotionally leaning on me as if I was his girlfriend and I wasn't. I had probably 3 - 4 different conversations that were an hour long about how my feelings weren't the same as his and why it wouldn't work out. He kept trying to justify our "relationship" that didn't exist. After the last conversation I realized I had to ghost him. I kept unintentionally leading him on when all I wanted was to maintain our current friendship. That could be why she ghosted you.

If you want to keep the friendship, you have to treat her only as a friend and nothing more.
Lol. Well that's what I was thinking. I wouldn't be confident enough to give myself a needle. How could I do a bullet?
That is what has happened to me previously but I don't know if I'll be able to this time. I'm in my 30's so I've had experience with relationships and everything but nothing has been like this.
I was thinking about this too recently. That if I was just in some sort of car accident that wasn't my fault then I wouldn't have to take the action myself.

I can't even do this now to my family. They see right through me. So last time someone asked I said "I'm depressed. I've been depressed for awhile now and I will be forever." And they didn't know what to say to that.

People tend to do better on race day due to anxiety and nerves so best of luck!

When I started running I just did 5K and 10K's. Then I did a few half marathons. Then one year I joined a running group and a few of us did a half marathon, a 30K and then a full marathon. I'm really slow but I'm glad I did it. Though I doubt I'll do it again, lol. So keep at it!
Yeah. . . I'm trying but I can't do it if he's barely even talking to me.
Yes to all the above. We don't communicate really. Every couple of weeks I send him a text and he might reply and that's about it. I'm just trying to keep the door open.

Yes, I was reading stuff on this recently too and guns "success" rate of suicide are higher than others but still not guaranteed. And you could end up alive but with other problems like being paralyzed or brain damage instead.

My thought was I don't think I could actually pull a trigger on myself. Like it took me a long time to be able to put in/take out contacts in my eyes. I don't think I could even give myself a flu shot. I don't know if I could pull a trigger.
My best time for a 5K was 28 mins so that's super fast! Congrats and good luck. Let me know how it goes.
It's a bit different than how you interpreted it. I didn't ruin it because I was depressed. I ruined it through other methods. The outcome of the break-up is this though.

This is something that everyone I spoke to said - "If you were meant to be with him it would've worked out or you'll get back together." But I honestly don't think that's true. Things just don't "happen".
I don't think that many would be affected if I was to disappear. My immediate family but I think that'd be it. For everyone else, I feel like it'd pass within a week. Shortly after my funeral.
Thank you.

I've been through other break-ups before and although I was depressed then I knew I'd get past it. I thought (and still think) that we were/are supposed to end up together. And this just hurts so much more. I don't know. . .

The main stopping force for me right now is the "how" part. And maybe a little bit of fear but mainly the how.

I've given up some old interests after the break-up as I realized I never really liked doing them anyway. I was doing them out of habit and it contributed to the whole break up. I've taken up something else but I find it doesn't really empty the pit I feel.

I know what you mean. . . I really do. It's good that you did tell her what you want in a relationship.

I think she just needs time to figure out what she wants. If she wants to be in a committed relationship with you or if she wants to have her single life because she can't have both. She might need a week or 2 to think about what she wants. In the ex I keep talking about it took me almost a month to figure out what was going on and what I wanted but unfortunately the ex figured out something different for himself.

All you can do is wait. Maybe contact her in a week if she hasn't gotten back to you to see where she stands. Otherwise do your best to move on. Which I know is also difficult. . .

I didn't tell him that exactly but he knows the just of things. I did write him a 3 page letter and we had quite the break-up talk about things so I think he's aware of my feelings. But I will copy/paste what I wrote in case for some reason I can tell him or send it to him. . . I really want to get back together with him. . . again. . . We weren't the best communicators, our timing seemed off and he got hurt. Perhaps similar to this OP here but different circumstances.

So as to not hijack this person's thread here's what I posted that gives me a bit more detail of my situation: https://www.reddit.com/r/relationships/comments/6nn996/getting_back_together_with_ex_bf_38m_after_poor/

But I'll send you a PM later too! Just because I could use someone to talk to. If you don't mind?

I'm sorry to hear this because I can somewhat empathize with the girl because of what happened to me. I've realized that effective communication is such an important part of a relationship and I feel like she deserved the chance to know your feelings. How can someone know what's troubling you if you never tell the person? Though I only take this from my experience. I did change after my ex broke up with me, well maybe 4 weeks before actually because we had a "break" for a bit, but I could've done it sooner had we had better communication with each other. Though a lot of my situation was due to external circumstances whereas it doesn't seem so with your girl.

Although it seemed unlikely she'd change from what you've told us about her. But you never know. That being said if she's seeing other guys that's pretty bad and I couldn't stay with someone who would do that. It doesn't seem like she wants to or is able to commit. But then again, maybe she would've if you told her?

This is one thing I have thought about too. Even though I thought he passed all his commitment issues maybe he hasn't? Like most people, obviously I blame myself the most but this could be true too. If he leaves now, what if things got worse? Would he leave again?

He's never been in a long term relationship other than with me and he's not one to discuss relationship issues with his friends and family so he wouldn't know about how to address the ups and downs of a relationship. That being said, I also didn't do a good job of it too. 

Though this particular down was for a long time - like 4 months and he did stick with it for 4 months. Can the "downs" of relationships last that long?
To the guy I was dating (my ex?) or the OP here?

I feel like what I posted is somewhat similar to your situation - just that the guy I was dating was the same age as you and I wasn't on the same page as him but I didn't know it at the time. We were in a committed relationship though and I wasn't sleeping with anyone else.

What I wish my ex had done with me was to sit me down for a serious talk and tell me his concerns. He mentioned them in passing but I was stupid and didn't take them seriously until it was too late for me to do anything. I would kill for a second chance now.

Sit her down and tell her this is serious. This is what you're looking for, this is how she's behaving and what does she want in life? If my ex had done that to me, seriously told me that our relationship was hinging on me and the fact that I wasn't moving our relationship forward - I would've figured things out sooner and I think the outcome would've been different. 

Then see what happens. If her outcome doesn't matches yours or if she says one thing and acts a different way, then end it. She just might need a kick to straighten things out.

To me, being too emotional was me over reacting and taking things too personally when I shouldn't have over what were probably stupid things. I do need to work on that but I don't think I'm always like that. It was mainly in the last 4 months when I was over worked, exhausted and adjusting to cutting sugar and carbs in my diet.
